author: @web_jar6630
body: Your point of having a barrier is an interesting one. However on the flip side (pun intended), screens on modern smartphones are getting really big and sometimes difficult to manage with one hand especially when you're travelling. I found the ability to use GMaps, music, calendar and basically any app on the outside screen extremely practical. The small form factor in the folded state doesn't make me constantly live in fear that my phone will fall out of my pocket or will get damaged when in my pocket. Maybe i'm a little biased but I actually like the feeling that I basically have no device in my pocket when I'm travelling while listening to music. But i also like that this device can also be used for reading, which I do think many people do. For example, going through rmails or news. With the normal form factor going over 6 inch screen for almost all devices, this flip style form factor is the only way to preserve practicality imo. For a much bigger screen, I have fond a dedicated tablet or a laptop to be a much better solution.

author: @neomancr
body:
After using ONE UI since the S7, it's virtually impossible to use vanilla android anymore. I'd love to be able to but it always feels like you're 5 years behind. Having to rely on AAudio, having to reach to the bottom of the phone to navigate where you can simply swipe from any side down to go home, back to go back, upward to split screen, back and held to swap between former apps, etc. All done without having to shift your hand.

Having a voice controller that can do anything you can do manually, or have it all automated based on space and time. Audio multitasking, being able to run multiple instances of the same app at once, even with 2 different IP addresses, having a secure Knox container air gapped from any android vulnerability, having something like an Alexa or Google home that's portable and able to take voice commands even while blasting music. Customizations that work better than Xposed framework without needing to root, all the capabilities to up cycle the device when it's through, leveraging dex and it's support for any USB device/ 24 bit audio and HDMI upscaled video where the phone and any screen can be used as a dual screen desktop setup. Inter operability between all galaxies, and so on and on.

I wish other phone labels would catch up and develop an android variant ad capable. Even galaxy watch has many more features and capabilities than other android watches.

Im surprised by how few Android devices can work as wifi repeaters and serve as hot spots with their own LAN. Apple level bg voice cancelation for calls using Samsung pro audio completely mutes all background sounds versus only suppressing them. But dex is a major one as is all the automation.

You can use all the tools to create something out of your phone that can do pretty much anything, even automatically serve as a red night light in your bedroom, play bedtime music, and slowly turn down the light and the music until you fall asleep.

Try using a Samsung foldable vs another foldable. Samsung have been doing split screen and multitasking for years before others have and have hardware optimized the back end to allow it to worn seamlessly. That's why dex came out and worked so smoothly without having to freeze inactive windows while a desktop mode has existed for AOSP for years hidden in developer settings but no one uses it

I bought it. I love it. Came from the iPhone 12 mini. Ive been on iPhone since the 3GS and im wondering why i didnt make the switch sooner. author: @krazybonnie5523
body:
I think part of the issue with the poor performance has to be the weak SoC.

The Dimensity 7400X performance is around the performance of SD860, which is a overclocked version of the SD855 which is in the S10 series of phones from 2019.

It is more efficient, but an efficient chip forced to run at high clocks won't be any more efficient that a more powerful chip running at much lower clocks. 

If Motorola raised the price by 50 to 100 and put in a proper Mid-range chip like Dimensity 8300 or 8400 & their derivatives, i think it would make a much better device.

The entire dimensity 6000 & 7000 chips are just really bad.

The 6000 chips are all derivatives of the low end Helios G99(from 2022)and the 7000s are very similar with the key change being a 1 to 2 generation newer ARM cores & GPU

author: @andyH_England
body:
It's good to see budget flip phones, although the premium versions are already poor value compared to candy bar phones in terms of specs at half the price. This Razr 2025 is articulated as 'you get what you pay for'. If you are a light casual user in a temperate climate, then this is a good test for whether you like flips -- I tried and it's not for me. I recommend instead buying a refurbished Flip 6, despite Samsung's QC seemingly on the decline as they save money. With the lack of demand for flips, already nearing their peak -- exactly as I expected, a niche product -- secondhand, their price is in freefall. Around £400 in the UK, which is £700 less than the launch price. You do have to hope that it survives to get some value for money, as the creaking screen is still a reminder of Samsung's flawed design choices.

There are too many compromises for this Razr to be suitable for a smartphone purist who expects to keep it for 3-5 years, if it can last that long. I doubt Lenovo makes money on these, and it's more of a spoiler to disrupt Samsung's flip sales, a party trick that Samsung has targeted rivals with for years.

body:
i wanted to trade my flip5 for the 2024 base razr
more battery life, less overheating, cheaper price? sounds perfect to me

but i wanted to know how it would hold up longterm. i have had the flips 3 4 and 5 and the hinge improvements on the 5 were phenomenal. i need to know whether the razr can stack up on physical durability (and not just the hinge- does that fake leather get grubby? does it start to peel away from the metal parts? etc)

id hate to trade in a solid phone thats lasted me two years for something that wont last a year

but i could not find a single review update from anyone that had used it for longer than a week! i want to hear from someone thats been using theirs this whole time on the daily
